## What you should be able to do tonight

- Define IC, IC decay, information ratio, quantile spread, turnover and capacity from memory, with a number for each of your signals.
- State the four assumptions of the fundamental law and which one fails hardest on your book.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>35 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Finish anything outstanding from days 169 to 174. The null distribution of mean IC is the piece worth having, because every signal from here is reported against it.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Closed book: the six definitions with your own numbers attached, and the four assumptions of the fundamental law. Say the whole thing out loud in under three minutes.

## Drill <span class='task-total'>interview thread</span>

Spaced repetition, not cramming. Every drill in the year is collected on the [drills page](../drills.qmd).

::: {.task-list .drill}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Arithmetic, timed, twenty-fifth sitting. Ten two-digit multiplications, the sevenths, and the square roots of 250, 500 and 1,000 to two decimals.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Order statistics with a decision attached: you interview candidates one at a time in random order and must hire on the spot. What policy maximises the chance of hiring the best, and what is that chance? State the threshold rule and the limiting probability.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> The trading version, which is how it is actually asked: you can trade once against a stream of quotes arriving in random order. When do you take one? Say why the answer is the same problem and what changes if you may take the second best.
:::
:::
